{"core_law": "Real breaking, cutting and digging all follow one budget: the useful part of a blow's energy pays for (1) the VOLUME that is crushed or pushed aside and (2) the new SURFACE of a crack or cut. E x eta = P x V + R x A, where E = energy of the blow (J, today's swing formula), eta = share that reaches the material (0.1-0.8), P = volume price (J/cm3, roughly 2-5 x the material's strength in MPa; pine 10, oak 27.5, granite 750, loam 0.04 - exactly the numbers POLUS already uses), V = removed volume (cm3), R = surface price (J/cm2 of new crack or cut face; glass 0.0008, granite 0.011, pine along grain 0.016 / across 0.18, leather ~1 [estimate], steel ~10), A = new surface (cm2). Plus one gate: the tool bites only if its pressure F/S reaches the material's hardness H (about 3 x strength, Tabor) and its edge is harder than the material; otherwise the edge dulls or bends and only a dent of V = E/H appears. The ratio l = R/P (a length) is the material's character: tiny l (glass 8 nm, granite ~0.1-0.7 um) = it cracks and shatters; big l (steel ~0.01-0.1 mm, leather, rubber ~0.5 mm) = it dents, tears, bends. A piece breaks off whenever a crack to a free face is cheaper than crushing it (d > ~6R/P). Sources: Atkins cutting model, Teale's law, Griffith, Tabor (see physics notes).
